points.description: States that infinite recursion can be caused by a missing base case (no terminating condition in the function).
States that infinite recursion can be caused by an incorrectly defined recursion step (the recursive call does not move toward the base case).
points.partial_credit: Half marks if stated vaguely, e.g. 'wrong recursive call' without saying it fails to progress toward the base case.

rubric.notes: Full marks need both causes: no base case, and an incorrect recursion step (call that doesn't progress toward the base case). Any wording is fine, e.g. 'no stopping condition'. If the student gives only one cause, give only that point's marks. Vague or partly right statements get half of that point. Answers about unrelated things, such as memory or syntax errors, get nothing.
